annotationRationale: Divisibility by 11 restricts the middle digit. Counting arrangements with repeated digits and leading-zero restrictions, then correcting for shared digit collections, gives the exhaustive four-case count.
sourceMethod: Followed the official partition of the 81 multiples into four digit-pattern cases. Added a proof that the middle digit is unique, justifying the pairing of distinct-digit multiples and preventing duplicate counts.

review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of official solution 25 on pages 9–10. It preserves all four categories and counts, while explaining why the middle digit is unique.
review.annotationCheck: Congruence and restricted multiset permutations are assessed; cnm_h232 supplies the supporting addition and multiplication rules.
